statement: A proportional–integral–derivative (PID) controller is a feedback control loop mechanism that continuously calculates an error value $e(t) = \mathrm{SP} - \mathrm{PV}(t)$ as the difference between a desired setpoint (SP) and a measured process variable (PV), and outputs a control variable $u(t)$. In parallel form, the control law is defined as $u(t) = K_p e(t) + K_i \int_{0}^{t} e(\tau)\,d\tau + K_d \frac{d}{dt}e(t) + u_0$, and in standard form as $u(t) = K_p \left(e(t) + \frac{1}{T_i} \int_{0}^{t} e(\tau)\,d\tau + T_d \frac{d}{dt}e(t)\right)$, where $K_i = K_p / T_i$ and $K_d = K_p T_d$. The supplied sources genuinely contain nothing to derive for the PID control law itself (nor any derivation using laplace_transform_of_derivative or partial_fractions), so it is presented as a definition.

properties.property: Relationship between standard and parallel form parameters: $K_i = K_p / T_i$ and $K_d = K_p T_d$ (or equivalently $T_i = K_p / K_i$ and $T_d = K_d / K_p$).
properties.why: Factoring the common gain $K_p$ out of the parallel form yields the standard form where $T_i$ and $T_d$ have physical interpretations as integral and derivative times.

properties.property: Laplace form transfer function: $G(s) = K_p + \frac{K_i}{s} + K_d s = \frac{K_d s^2 + K_p s + K_i}{s}$.
properties.why: Represents the proportional, integral ($1/s$), and derivative ($s$) actions on the error signal in the frequency domain.

properties.property: Series (interacting) form representation: $G(s) = K_c \left(\frac{1}{\tau_i s} + 1\right)(\tau_d s + 1)$ with $K_p = K_c \alpha$, $T_i = \tau_i \alpha$, $T_d = \tau_d / \alpha$, and $\alpha = 1 + \frac{\tau_d}{\tau_i}$.
properties.why: Consists of a PI and PD controller in series, enabling tracking of an external bias value for multi-controller schemes.

properties.property: Proportional band representation: proportional gain can be expressed in reciprocal form as the proportional band $100 / K_p$.
properties.why: Represents the range of the process variable over which the output changes from 0% to 100% before saturating.

properties.property: Formulation basing derivative and proportional action on PV: $\mathrm{MV}(t) = K_p \left(-PV(t) + \frac{1}{T_i} \int_{0}^{t} e(\tau)\,d\tau - T_d \frac{d}{dt}PV(t)\right)$.
properties.why: Eliminates unwanted output spikes and large instant changes caused by step changes in the setpoint.

properties.property: Backward-difference discrete recurrence relation: $u(t_k) = u(t_{k-1}) + \left(K_p + K_i \Delta t + \frac{K_d}{\Delta t}\right) e(t_k) + \left(-K_p - \frac{2K_d}{\Delta t}\right) e(t_{k-1}) + \frac{K_d}{\Delta t} e(t_{k-2})$.
properties.why: Obtained by differentiating the continuous PID equation with respect to time and replacing continuous derivatives with backward finite differences.

properties.property: Z-transform discrete IIR form: $C(z) = \frac{\left(K_p + K_i \Delta t + \frac{K_d}{\Delta t}\right) + \left(-K_p - \frac{2K_d}{\Delta t}\right) z^{-1} + \frac{K_d}{\Delta t} z^{-2}}{1 - z^{-1}}$.
properties.why: Expresses the discrete backward-difference PID algorithm as an infinite impulse response digital filter in the Z-domain.

assumptions.assumption: The setpoint SP is constant or smooth when derivative action is based directly on error $e(t)$.
assumptions.breaks_when: The setpoint undergoes an abrupt step change, causing a large unwanted derivative spike (derivative kick) in the controller output.

assumptions.assumption: The controller output operates within the linear, unsaturated range of the actuator (e.g., 0% to 100%).
assumptions.breaks_when: The process variable deviates outside the proportional band $100/K_p$, driving the output into full-off or full-on actuator saturation.

assumptions.assumption: In discrete implementations, the loop interval time $\Delta t$ is strictly constant and small relative to process dynamics.
assumptions.breaks_when: Algorithm execution time or system pre-emption delays loop execution beyond $\Delta t$.

assumptions.assumption: The actuator and process variable units are dimensionless fractions or are scaled by appropriate conversion factors in $K_p, K_i, K_d$.
assumptions.breaks_when: The actuator and measured values are in different physical units without unit conversion factors applied to the gains.

failure_modes.signature: A large, unwanted spike or impulse in the controller output $u(t)$ immediately upon a setpoint change.
failure_modes.cause: Differentiating an error signal $e(t) = \mathrm{SP} - \mathrm{PV}$ that contains step discontinuities from changing the setpoint.

failure_modes.signature: An instant, potentially very large step change in output $u(t)$ when the setpoint is altered.
failure_modes.cause: Proportional action directly responding to a discontinuous jump in the error signal rather than being based on PV.

failure_modes.signature: Output clamps at 0% or 100% and ceases to respond linearly to changes in error.
failure_modes.cause: The error moves outside the proportional band $100/K_p$ or persistent error integration drives the command to physical limits.

failure_modes.signature: Erratic or degraded regulation and inaccurate numerical differentiation/integration.
failure_modes.cause: Relying on a fixed wait(dt) that fails to account for algorithm execution duration or thread pre-emption delays.
